conditional_findings.classification: Recovered059 Segovb SurfaceVertices array-admission question newly reassessed at95e; no new historical finding or checkpoint3821 attribution.
conditional_findings.canonical_owner: The serialized PreparedCityGround SurfaceVertices arrays and their worker-product-to-native-Mesh admission boundary.
conditional_findings.first_failed_contract: Derived deserialization admits each packed vertex buffer independently, while the normal producer relies on their equal lengths and complete triangle groups before a usable Mesh is built.
conditional_findings.trace: Segovb Lens12 READ527 at6533 already distinguished the normal single-point producer loop, which appends all five arrays together, from independent derived Deserialize fields and left receiver/native admission and actual reachability open. At95e the binary field decoder rejects bytes that end within an element but does not compare sibling arrays or enforce complete triangles. wasm_receive_job passes bytes to worker_products::receive; after CBOR decoding it checks the ticket owner and RegionalCity product document/graphics identity, then stages the product without a SurfaceVertices aggregate check. SurfaceVertices::build inserts the arrays into a TriangleList mesh. PreparedCityGround::meshes caches its result separately per presentation owner and the map path passes the mesh through geographic_ground::reflected.
conditional_findings.symbolic_example: For a hypothetical otherwise valid product with three positions, two normals and three UV, footprint and activity entries, each packed field has a whole number of elements (36,24,24,48,24 bytes respectively). Assuming CBOR shape, ticket, document and graphics are otherwise valid, the inspected field-level decoder has no cross-array rejection and the identity check does not inspect these lengths. The exact Cargo.lock-pinned Bevy Mesh source counts the minimum attribute length, here2; reflected then constructs indices0..2, and pinned invert_winding returns AbruptIndicesEnd for a TriangleList index count not divisible by3. The per-owner OnceLock stores that error. These are source expressions and symbolic counts only; no payload, decoding, mesh, worker, asset or runtime was created.
conditional_findings.counterevidence: The normal in-process builder appends all five arrays in one point loop, so its own generated geometry is correlated. IndexedDB entries are gzip size-bounded and checked by a content checksum; cache keys include format, executable revision and job. The ordinary worker generates and serializes its own product before receipt, and the client rejects decode errors and document/graphics mismatches. No supported normal producer emitting mismatched arrays, stale cache, corruption, hostile message, actual error or persistent failure was observed. A self-consistent hypothetical payload is a conditional admission question, not proof a checksum-valid cache becomes corrupt.
conditional_findings.consumer_qualification: The JS cache retry for decode/mismatch is around wasm_receive_job; a later hypothetical map winding failure is classified at focused installation, after the receipt stage, and the inspected source does not show that retry handling it. Focused installation reports a ground error and despawns its just-created root on failure; asset lifetime and user-visible behavior remain open.
